surfaces.name: manifest
surfaces.notes: The compatibility tag itself; it must be restored together with the state it describes. Nothing is rewritten while the tag is in force, so the first tagging wins. This package writes it only to tag a directory that predates it.

surfaces.name: workgraph
surfaces.notes: Generation CAS under <path>.lock, then an fsx atomic replace; the .bak is read only while the main file is absent. Factures (failure classes), evidence, artifacts, step budgets and mission revisions are fields of this document, not separate files: restoring the file restores all of them, and its generation CAS refuses a stale writer.

surfaces.name: pauses
surfaces.version: 1 (pauseStoreVersion; any other value is refused, never coerced)
surfaces.notes: Cross-process lock plus atomic replace, re-read from disk on every access. An operator stop: restoring it is restoring a stop request that was already in force, and dropping it would silently resume work nobody asked to resume.

surfaces.name: controls
surfaces.notes: Cross-process lock plus atomic replace; the event array is append-only and only lifecycle fields mutate, and the operator mailbox (questions) travels in the same document with its own sequence. MissionRevision lives here and in workgraph node fields. Controls and questions received after the checkpoint are NOT undone by restoring this file: they must be reconciled from durable history (H4 requirement).

surfaces.name: decisions
surfaces.notes: Append under <path>.lock with repair of an incomplete final line. No generation: a rollback may only truncate at a durable line boundary, and a complete-but-unterminated final value is completed rather than discarded.

surfaces.name: session-catalog
surfaces.notes: Atomic replace under sessions/.session-catalog.lock. Names the roots of a session, so a restored catalog that omits a root makes an existing mission unreachable.

surfaces.name: session-ledger
surfaces.notes: Append with tail repair and no CAS. The conversation history: a crash can leave a zero-filled tail, which is failed closed rather than replayed.

surfaces.name: legacy-ledger
surfaces.notes: Flat pre-catalog layout, copied once into sessions/<id>/ and never written again. Present only in state directories created before the session catalog existed; restoring it is restoring a migration source.

surfaces.name: legacy-session
surfaces.notes: Monolithic pre-0.2 transcript, read once and migrated into sessions/<id>/nodes/ with the source preserved; the marker .legacy-migrated gates the replay. Never restored: it is a migration source, not live state.

surfaces.name: session-nodes
surfaces.notes: Per-file lock <n>.json.lock with Generation++ under it and an fsx atomic replace; transcript writes compare the message hash before replacing. A restored transcript must still satisfy the hash a live writer expects (CompareAndSetMessages, same file:244), or the write is refused rather than merged.

surfaces.name: compaction-archives
surfaces.version: none; the file name IS the message hash
surfaces.notes: Recovery material for a compacted transcript, content-addressed: a name collision with different content is refused. A restore is a no-op and a rewrite is a corruption.

surfaces.name: compaction-leases
surfaces.notes: A heartbeat keeps the lock fresh while its owner lives; a lock older than 30s is treated as an owner that died. Liveness, not state: restoring a snapshot must never restore a lease whose owner is gone, and the stale window is the recovery path.

surfaces.name: summary-cache
surfaces.version: none; the key is the transcript hash + model + summary budget
surfaces.writer: internal/contextwindow cache, rooted by the session catalog
surfaces.notes: Content-keyed atomic replace per key. Derived: dropping or restoring it only changes token cost, never meaning - which is also why it must not be treated as evidence.

surfaces.name: grants
surfaces.notes: Atomic replace under the permission engine lock. Operator approval memory: restoring it would re-grant a permission that was revoked afterwards, so it stays out of a checkpoint.

surfaces.name: workspace-index
surfaces.version: 1 (snapshotVersion; any other value is refused and the index rebuilt)
surfaces.notes: Rebuilt from the tree through an atomic replace. One of the few surfaces with its own version discriminator, and the model the rest of the manifest generalizes.

surfaces.name: tool-results
surfaces.format: mixed (spilled tool output, text or binary)
surfaces.notes: Write-once per name through an fsx atomic replace. Referenced by evidence artifacts: restoring a state image without them leaves evidence dangling, which must be reported rather than silently accepted.

surfaces.name: reports
surfaces.notes: Write-once per node/root, no lock. Derived prose rendered from durable state: it is never authority for a mission.

surfaces.name: background-receipts
surfaces.version: none; the decoder also accepts the older fixed-array shape
surfaces.notes: Atomic replace per job id. A restored receipt can name a process that no longer exists: the manager must reconcile it, never trust a PID from a snapshot. This surface already widened its accepted shape once (it now also decodes the older fixed-array form) with nothing on disk recording the change; the manifest makes the next such change visible.

surfaces.name: background-logs
surfaces.notes: Output of a background process. The read side checks the size and OutputSHA256 against the receipt, so a truncated restore is detected instead of being served as complete output.

surfaces.name: migration-markers
surfaces.notes: Created once after a one-way migration completes; presence means do not migrate again. .session-catalog-migrated, .flat-session-layout-migrated, .legacy-migrated, plus .flat-layout-migration.sha256. Restoring a snapshot without them replays a migration that already ran.

surfaces.name: locks-and-temp
surfaces.notes: Locks carry a pid/created/token and a heartbeat; the temp files are created by AtomicWriteFile and removed by it. Never part of a snapshot: a restored stale lock or .bak silently changes which copy a writer trusts, so these are deleted, not restored.

surfaces.name: permissions
surfaces.notes: Loaded once through permission.LoadRules. Operator authority, not mission state: a rollback must not revert a rule change.

surfaces.name: lsp-config
surfaces.notes: Read when the LSP manager starts. Configuration of an external tool, not progress.

surfaces.name: provider-profiles
surfaces.notes: Discovery order is explicit directory, then install, then unified user config, then legacy providers only. Installation configuration deliberately outside the workspace (the edited project is not a profile source). A checkpoint must never restore it: it holds credentials and may rotate between launches.

surfaces.name: project-config
surfaces.writer: internal/skills and internal/instructions readers (operator or model authors)
surfaces.notes: Loaded per turn, not cached. Configuration, not mission progress: a rollback must not silently revert an instruction the operator edited.

surfaces.name: lifecycle-journal
surfaces.path: <supervisor root>/journal.json (chosen by the supervisor, never inside the candidate state)
surfaces.notes: H1: an fsx lock plus revision CAS plus atomic replace, with active/known-good/checkpoint/receipts in ONE file and no second pointer write. It must stay outside the state image so that the record of a rollback cannot itself be rewritten by that rollback.

surfaces.name: versions-store
surfaces.version: hash-named; the directory name is the artifact hash
surfaces.notes: H3: an immutable publish, then a pointer file swapped only after the gate. Launched by path and never replaced in place (a running .exe cannot be replaced on Windows); hashes are verified before every launch.
